tldr: Markets whipsawed violently: Wednesday's huge post-midterm relief rally fully reversed Thursday -- S&P -4.36%, Nasdaq -5.52% (correction), VIX +69.7% to 28.18 -- on an AI-capex political-risk shock (Texas governor-elect campaigning to pause data-center construction), not fresh economic data.
Today's Oct NFP (21:30 SGT, consensus 65K vs Sept's 29K miss) is the single most important catalyst of the day, landing on top of hawkish Fed speak that's pushed December-hike odds to ~68-73%.

The levered-silver sleeve underperformed gold Thursday (SLV -0.5%, SILJ -1.6%, HL -3.3% vs GLD +0.8%) purely on silver's industrial-metal beta to the tech selloff -- Kitco confirms no silver-specific catalyst, so this reads as noise, not a thesis break.

HK tech rallied hard (Tencent +7.2%, Xiaomi +8.8%) on a US-AI-regulation rotation trade, but Southbound Stock Connect sold a net -HK$21.3bn into that same rally (the largest outflow in 7 months) -- mainland money took profit rather than confirming the move.

Data-quality flag: the price feed's "GOLD" instrument is NOT Barrick (Barrick re-ticked to NYSE:B in 2025); its -9.46% Thursday move belongs to an unrelated company, Gold.com Inc, and should not be read as a mining-sector signal.

Rare-earth basket diverged sharply: Lynas +8.0% on its own record quarterly print while MP (-6.0%) and Energy Fuels (-8.2%) fell on the US-China truce reducing near-term supply-crunch urgency plus a real Energy Fuels earnings miss.

regime.label: Hawkish-Fed AI-capex de-rating / two-way whipsaw
regime.oneLiner: A market that priced in election-clarity relief on Wednesday repriced AI-capex political risk and a hawkish Fed on Thursday, erasing the entire rally in one session ahead of today's make-or-break NFP print.

topNews.headline: US stocks post biggest selloff of the year as AI-capex political-risk fears erase the entire post-midterm relief rally
topNews.actionable: No direct AI-hardware exposure in this book, but the ~6:1 negative NYSE breadth means little was spared, including the levered-silver and HK-tech sleeves -- today's NFP is the next test of whether this extends or reverses.

topNews.headline: Southbound Stock Connect sees largest outflow in 7 months (-HK$21.3bn) even as HK tech rallies -- mainland investors took profit, didn't chase
topNews.actionable: A durability flag, not a confirmation, for the owner's 0700/0981/1810 exposure -- watch whether Southbound flow turns net positive again before trusting Thursday's price strength.

topNews.headline: Silver and miners underperform gold as a high-beta spillover from the tech selloff, not a metals-specific event
topNews.actionable: Thursday's levered-silver underperformance tracked the broad equity rout rather than signaling fresh metals-specific weakness -- today's NFP is the next real test of the thesis.

topNews.headline: Rare-earth basket diverges sharply: Lynas +8% on its own record quarterly update while MP (-6%) and Energy Fuels (-8%) fall on US-truce and earnings-miss reasons
topNews.actionable: The ex-China basket is not trading as one block right now -- company-specific catalysts (Lynas beat, Energy Fuels miss) matter as much as the shared China-truce-expiry overhang into Nov 10.

topNews.headline: US October nonfarm payrolls due today 21:30 SGT, consensus 65K after September's steep 29K miss -- the key swing catalyst
topNews.actionable: The single most important scheduled data point for this portfolio today -- a soft print could revive rate-cut hope and lift both equities and gold/silver; a hot print risks extending Thursday's selloff.

signals: SLV/GLD model priors moved apart this run (SLV pUp3m 0.56 vs GLD 0.62) on the industrial-beta-vs-safe-haven divergence seen Thursday -- worth watching whether silver re-couples to gold once the equity whipsaw settles.

Lynas (LYC.AX) is now the highest-confidence call in the rare-earth basket (0.5) after a company-specific quarterly beat, while Energy Fuels (UUUU) is the highest-confidence decline (0.45) after a real earnings miss and analyst downgrade -- consider watching for basket-wide re-correlation around the Nov 10 China-truce deadline.

USD/Cash is the only asset class upgraded to modest OW this run -- the model reads cash as the best tactical ballast into today's NFP and the Dec 11 government-funding cliff, not a directional call on any one asset.

MU (Micron) remains a crowded multi-investor consensus trade (Congress, Soros, ETFs all bought the same week) that still sold off Nov 4 -- a reminder that convergence doesn't protect against a single bad session, relevant context given Thursday's broader AI-capex-driven chip selloff.

Korea's KOSPI -5.28% Thursday on direct Samsung/SK hynix selling confirms the AI-capex-regulation fear is a regional semiconductor-sector event, not a US-isolated one -- worth watching for read-through to SMIC (0981.HK) given its relative resilience (+2.28%) so far.
